::: {.grid-intro}
The Global RIver-lanD (GRID) project connects river hydrogeochemical observations with watershed information to support research on weathering, water quality, and river biogeochemical cycles.

Explore released datasets, analysis code, teaching resources, and opportunities to collaborate.
:::

:::

These totals describe the assembled GRID inventory. Individual releases cover specific subsets. Not every hydrogeochemical variable or watershed property is available at every site. [View coverage and contents](database/coverage.qmd).

## Featured research output

::: {.release-feature}
### River weathering data and machine-learning workflows

An August 2026 GRID output connects river chemistry and watershed context with geochemical inverse modeling and machine-learning analysis across the contiguous United States.

[Explore the data and code release](database/highlights/weathering-ml-2026.qmd)
:::

## Help shape the next stage

GRID-SI is a proposed development program to improve chemistry documentation, catchment links, and reusable workflows. [Read the development roadmap](development.qmd) or [discuss a contribution](get-involved.qmd).
